Date: 2026-04-02 15:30 UTC | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Tomás Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Nova), Daniel Brooks (Nova), Sara Nguyen (Nova)

Links shared: deck: https://redwood.app/decks/poc-capacity-playbook (placeholder), benchmark sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/benchmark-nova (placeholder), security packet: s3://redwood-sec-packets/nova/soc2.pdf

Transcript: (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect)

00:00 Maya: okay hi everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account, quick intros?
00:07 Priya: hey im Priya, head of ML at Nova, we own the model infra and the user-facing endpoints, thanks for running these POC talks.
00:12 Daniel: Daniel, platform eng, I'll be the primary infra contact.
00:15 Sara: Sara, CTO, just here for high level context.
00:18 Tomás: Tomas Rivera, solutions eng at Redwood - I'll own the benchmark plan and run coordination.
00:23 Maya: Great, goal today is lock down sizing and autoscale approach for your POC, confirm success criteria and timeline.
01:10 Priya: to start, our workload - mostly chat completions with a median seq len ~128 tokens, 95th around 600, and we have spiky qps peaks when batch jobs finish, like up to 450 concurrent reqs for a few minutes. Average sustained qps about 18rps.
01:35 Tomás: okay that's helpful. So two dimensions: steady-state baseline (sustained 18 qps) and peak burst for short windows. For reserved capacity we recommend sizing for the steady-state plus a safety buffer and use burst pools to absorb peaks.
02:02 Daniel: curious — what does burst mean operationally? are those preemptible nodes or reserved warm GPUs?
02:10 Tomás: good question. For Redwood Dedicated we do reserved GPU pools (pinned to the customer) and a burst pool that can be either pre-warmed reserved or a shared burst tier that spins up across region — for POC we often do a small reserved pool + staged burst where we allow fallback to hosted pool if private burst is saturated. The fallback could be to a lower-cost model variant to preserve latency SLOs.
02:38 Priya: fallback to hosted raises data residency / security flags for us, Nova is pretty strict — can't send PII outside our VPC.
02:46 Maya: understood. We can do private burst in your VPC via Redwood Private, or we can configure model-level fallbacks that stay within your private deployment — e.g., quantized variant of same model on reserve. We'll include KMS/HSM integration notes in the security packet.
03:10 Sara: what's the expected p95 latency on the benchmarks you run? we have target of p95 < 300ms for interactive use.
03:20 Tomás: If you want p95 < 300ms for seq lengths up to 256, we typically size GPUs such that steady-state is handled with headroom — that usually ends up being N GPUs. Quick ballpark: with a Llama2-variant 13B fp16 on A100-ish hardware you might get ~40-80 tokens/s per GPU depending on batch config; with continuous batching we can push throughput but latency tradeoffs need tuned batch windows. For your profile, I'd ballpark 3-4 reserved GPUs for steady-state with burst capacity to handle peaks. But we'll validate in bench run.
04:02 Daniel: can you explain continuous batching? we run k8s with istio ingress so per-request latency has to be predictable.
04:10 Tomás: sure - continuous batching groups inflight requests to amortize kernel cost; it's latency sensitive but we tune max grouping window (e.g., 10-20ms) so tail latency stays acceptable. We also do prefix/KV cache to avoid re-computing prefixes for similar prompts — that's big win for chat flows.
04:45 Priya: KV cache — is that stateful? do we need sticky sessions?
04:50 Tomás: it's KV cache per model instance; you can configure sticky routing or shared KV store; for the POC we can start with sticky routing to keep it simple. That will influence autoscale because cached contexts are not available instantly to new nodes.
05:20 Maya: note: sticky routing increases cold-start tail; part of the POC evaluation is to measure cold-start penalties when scale-out occurs versus overprovisioning reserved nodes.
05:40 Priya: okay, success criteria — for us: 1) p95 latency under 300ms for seq up to 256, 2) cost per 1M tokens below our threshold (we gave a ballpark in the RFP), 3) no cross-region data egress (all in VPC), 4) autoscale behavior graceful with <2% error rate during bursts. Does that align?
06:12 Tomás: yes that's a clear set. We'll add exact benchmark tests to validate each. For cost target we'll simulate traffic for 72 hours at scaled pattern to estimate unit economics.
06:28 Daniel: how do you measure cost in the POC? do you show per-token breakdown?
06:33 Maya: Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdown; for POC we can provide a blinded financials sheet showing reserved vs hosted unit cost, include amortized GPU hours, plus assumptions about bin packing / utilization.
06:50 Priya: timeline — we want POC to start mid-April, 6 weeks total: week 1 infra & baseline, week 2 bench runs, week 3 tuning, weeks 4-5 production shadow and extended peak tests, week 6 handoff + acceptance. Workable?
07:10 Maya: yes mid-April start is doable. We'll lock dates after benchmark scheduling.
07:20 Tomás: for the benchmark plan I'll propose three test cases: a) steady-state 18 qps for 24h; b) spike tests — ramp to 450 concurrent for 5-10m repeated 6 times in a day; c) long tail tests with 95th seq 600 tokens to see latency degradation. We'll instrument p50/p95/p99 and error rate.
08:05 Daniel: what's the rollback / fallback policy if burst saturates? we prefer automatic fallback over request failing.
08:12 Tomás: default policy: when reserved + private burst saturated, route to a quantized model variant within same VPC (if available) or queue requests briefly — we can configure graceful degradation: reduce max response length, call a smaller model (like 7B q4_0) or return cached response. We'll show lat/quality tradeoffs in the plan.
08:38 Priya: quality degradation to smaller model concerns product — we need to measure user-visible delta. Can you add eval prompts to the bench that score outputs against a golden set?
08:47 Tomás: absolutely — we'll include a small eval harness with labeled prompts and automated BLEU/ROUGE-ish and human sampling to estimate drift.
09:05 Sara: what about autoscale latency — if you spin up new nodes how long until they're warm and ready?
09:12 Tomás: cold start depends on model size and whether KV cache and weights are preloaded; we can pre-warm by keeping a small standby pool or use warm images so typical cold-start is 30-90s on bigger models; with pre-warming you can get it below 20s. For POC we usually pre-warm a tiny fraction to keep cold starts infrequent.
09:40 Daniel: how do you handle predictability vs cost? we can't keep too many warm nodes because budget.
09:46 Maya: that's the heart of the POC — we compare strategies: reserve enough GPUs for baseline + small warm pool; enable burst with controlled maximum; set auto-fallback thresholds (e.g. queue depth or latency crossing threshold) to switch model variant. The POC reports will include cost per strategy.
10:05 Priya: for reserved GPUs, do you support specific instance types? we are planning to use on-prem with A10G class cards.
10:12 Tomás: yes Redwood Private supports a range of hardware; our runtime picks kernels based on arch. For A10G-ish performance we'll adjust batch sizes; we'll validate in bench. Please include exact GPU SKU in the infra doc.
10:30 Daniel: we run Kubernetes on-prem — how does Redwood integrate?
10:36 Maya: Two options: 1) Redwood Private lightweight control plane that orchestrates local inference pods, or 2) deploy Redwood runtime as container images under your K8s with our operator. Both can integrate with your KMS and logging. For POC we recommend operator mode for faster iteration.
11:00 Priya: security question — audit logs and SSO? we need SAML SSO, detailed audit logs, and key rotation via Azure Key Vault.
11:09 Maya: we support SAML/SSO, RBAC, and KMS integrations incl Azure Key Vault. Audit logs can be delivered to your ELK stack or S3. We'll add config examples in the security packet.
11:25 Sara: any blockers on our side to start mid-April?
11:28 Daniel: we'll need to carve a VPC and provide service account creds, plus a small sample of production traffic (anonymized) for bench. Also procurement needs a SOW.
11:38 Maya: we'll provide a draft SOW and POC SOW template.
11:44 Tomás: back to numbers — can we commit to a bench target for 95th latency and error rate? we'll aim for p95<300ms and error rate <0.5% for steady-state; during bursts the p95 might increase but fallback should keep error rate below 2%. Put that in success criteria.
12:12 Priya: acceptable. Also include quality threshold for model fallbacks: we want average semantic similarity >0.85 on our eval set.
12:30 Tomás: noted. We'll include automated eval metrics.

-- Mid-call interruptions & imperfect transcribing --

14:05 Speaker 1: hey can you explain the kv cache a gain, I think I missed a bit? (overlap)
14:12 Tomás: yeah, so kv cache stores past key/value tensors for recently seen tokens so repeated prefixes don't require recompute, it's huge for chat.
14:30 Priya: will sticky routing require session affinity on the ingress?
14:34 Tomás: yes, or a shared cache solution, but sticky is simplest for POC.

20:00 Maya: we also recommend run a quick micro-benchmark for model variants (13B full precision, 13B q4_0, 7B q4_0) to quantify cost vs latency vs quality.
20:27 Daniel: and what about autoscale thresholds? are those reactive or predictive?
20:33 Tomás: both. We'll test reactive thresholds (cpu/gpu utilization, queue depth) and a simple predictive buffer based on short-term qps slope to reduce cold starts. We'll measure false positive scale-outs.
21:00 Priya: what monitoring will we get? per-request trace?
21:05 Maya: Redwood Console gives per-route traces, token-level latency, token costs, and error logs; we'll hook into your datadog or prometheus as needed.
21:30 Daniel: any compliance issues with storing KV cache in our environment?
21:36 Tomás: it's ephemeral and can be disabled; if you need strict control we can encrypt and ensure cache doesn't persist to disk.
22:00 Priya: ok next steps recap?
22:05 Maya: Recap: Redwood sends POC pricing + SOW + security packet; Tomás sends bench plan and eval harness; Daniel provides infra creds and traffic sample; we schedule the 2-hour bench run for next Tuesday (2026-04-07) subject to infra ready.
22:30 Sara: sounds good, thanks.
22:40 Maya: any last questions?
22:43 Priya: none. thanks everyone.
22:47 Maya: we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.

- Success metrics: p95 < 300ms (seq up to 256), error rate <0.5% steady, fallback error rate <2%, quality similarity >0.85 for fallbacks, cost per 1M tokens below Nova threshold
